task_summary: Implement a React + TypeScript + Vite frontend SPA for a task management application. The SPA communicates with a FastAPI backend, exposing CRUD operations on tasks plus a health check endpoint. The component must define 11+ types, an API client layer, error handling utilities, and React components (App, TaskList, TaskItem, TaskForm, StatusBadge). Files must stay under 300 lines; composition over inheritance is mandated.

findings.finding: The standard pattern for React SPAs is to isolate all fetch/axios calls into a dedicated api.ts module that returns typed responses. This decouples UI components from transport concerns. Use a single base‐URL resolver (reading from import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL with a sensible fallback like '' for same-origin or 'http://localhost:8000') and a shared error-parsing function. Prefer native fetch over axios to minimize bundle size unless interceptors or cancellation are heavily needed.
findings.source: React community conventions; Vite documentation on env variables (import.meta.env.VITE_* prefix required)
findings.relevance: Directly maps to resolveBaseUrl(), parseErrorResponse(), and the five API functions in the spec.

findings.finding: Define types in a dedicated types.ts file. Use 'type' for data shapes (Task, TaskCreateRequest, etc.) and 'enum' (or const object + type union) for TaskStatus. Branded types (type TaskId = number & { __brand: 'TaskId' }) are overkill here; a simple 'type TaskId = number' (or string if UUID) suffices. Use discriminated unions for API error responses when multiple error shapes exist.
findings.relevance: Covers all 16+ types in the spec. Keeping types in one file keeps them under 300 lines given the count.

findings.finding: For a single-resource CRUD app, useState + useEffect in the App component is sufficient; no external state library needed. Pattern: tasks state array, loading boolean, error state. Optimistic updates improve UX but add complexity—for an initial implementation, refetch-after-mutate (call fetchTasks after create/update/delete) is simpler and correct. Use useCallback for handlers passed to child components to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
findings.source: React documentation (react.dev); Kent C. Dodds patterns
findings.relevance: Directly governs App.handleCreate, App.handleUpdate, App.handleDelete, App.useEffectFetchOnMount.

findings.finding: Recommended structure: src/types.ts, src/api.ts, src/App.tsx, src/components/TaskList.tsx, src/components/TaskItem.tsx, src/components/TaskForm.tsx, src/components/StatusBadge.tsx. Props interfaces (TaskListProps, TaskItemProps, TaskFormProps) should be co-located with their components or in types.ts. This keeps every file well under 300 lines.
findings.source: Vite React template conventions; Bulletproof React architecture guide
findings.relevance: Directly satisfies the 300-line file limit and composition-over-inheritance standard.

findings.finding: parseErrorResponse should handle: (1) non-OK responses with JSON body conforming to ErrorResponse, (2) non-OK responses with non-JSON body (network proxy errors, 502s), (3) network failures (TypeError from fetch). Return a normalized ApiError struct in all cases. Display errors in UI via an error state rendered as a dismissible banner.
findings.source: MDN Fetch API documentation; OWASP frontend error handling guidelines
findings.relevance: Maps to parseErrorResponse() and the ErrorResponse / ApiError types. This is the most commonly under-implemented area in task-management SPAs.

findings.finding: React's JSX auto-escapes string interpolation, mitigating most XSS. Avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML entirely. Validate/constrain task input on the form (maxLength, required fields) to provide defense-in-depth alongside backend validation. Use HTTPS in production; configure CORS on the backend side (not frontend concern, but resolveBaseUrl must not hardcode http:// in prod).
findings.source: OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet; React security documentation
findings.relevance: TaskForm handles user input that flows to the API; proper constraints prevent malformed data and reduce attack surface.

findings.finding: Vite exposes env vars prefixed with VITE_ on import.meta.env. Define an ImportMetaEnv interface extending ImportMeta to get type safety. The resolveBaseUrl function should read import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? '' and strip trailing slashes. At build time these are statically replaced, so they cannot be changed post-build without rebuild or a runtime config endpoint.
findings.relevance: Directly implements resolveBaseUrl() and ImportMetaEnv type from the spec.

findings.topic: Common Pitfalls: useEffect Cleanup and Race Conditions
findings.finding: The fetchOnMount useEffect must handle component unmount during in-flight requests. Use an AbortController signal passed to fetch, and abort in the cleanup function. Alternatively, use a boolean 'ignore' flag. Without this, setting state on an unmounted component causes warnings and potential bugs in StrictMode (which double-invokes effects in dev).
findings.source: React documentation on synchronizing with effects; Dan Abramov's 'A Complete Guide to useEffect'

findings.finding: The operating procedures mandate backend tests but do not explicitly mandate frontend unit tests. However, the API client functions (api.ts) are pure async functions and are trivially testable with vitest + msw (Mock Service Worker) or simple fetch mocking. Component tests with @testing-library/react are recommended for TaskForm (submit behavior) and TaskList (rendering). Vitest is the natural choice with Vite.
findings.source: Vitest documentation; Testing Library best practices
findings.relevance: While not strictly required by the operating procedures (which specify pytest for backend), having frontend tests improves reliability. At minimum, the api.ts functions warrant tests.

findings.finding: For a small task list (<1000 items), performance is not a concern. However, best practice dictates: use React.memo on TaskItem if the list grows, use stable keys (task.id, not array index) in list rendering, and memoize handlers with useCallback. Avoid creating new object/function references in JSX props inside map loops—instead, pass id and let child call parent handler.
findings.source: React performance documentation; React DevTools Profiler guidance
findings.relevance: Affects TaskList/TaskItem rendering pattern. Using task.id as key is critical for correct reconciliation during updates and deletes.

findings.finding: For TaskForm, prefer controlled components (useState per field) for simple forms. Libraries like react-hook-form are warranted for complex validation but overkill for 2-3 fields (title, description, status). The form should support both create mode (empty initial state) and edit mode (pre-populated from existing Task). Distinguish modes via presence of an initial task prop.
findings.source: React documentation on forms; react-hook-form docs for comparison
findings.relevance: TaskFormProps likely includes an optional onSubmit callback and optional initial Task. Keeps implementation simple and under 300 lines.

findings.finding: DeleteConfirmation type suggests the API returns a confirmation object. The UI should show a confirmation dialog (window.confirm or a modal component) before calling deleteTask. After successful deletion, remove the task from local state. Handle 404 gracefully (task already deleted by another client).
findings.source: UX best practices for destructive actions; Nielsen Norman Group guidelines
findings.relevance: Directly affects App.handleDelete implementation and the user-facing delete flow.

recommended_approach:
**File Structure:**
```
src/
  types.ts          — All type definitions (TaskId, TaskStatus, Task, request/response types, prop types, ImportMetaEnv)
  api.ts            — resolveBaseUrl(), parseErrorResponse(), fetchTasks(), createTask(), updateTask(), deleteTask(), healthCheck()
  App.tsx           — Root component with state, handlers, useEffect fetch-on-mount
  components/
    TaskList.tsx    — Renders list of TaskItem components
    TaskItem.tsx    — Single task display with edit/delete actions
    TaskForm.tsx    — Controlled form for create/edit
    StatusBadge.tsx — Status enum → colored badge mapping using StatusBadgeColorMap
  env.d.ts          — ImportMetaEnv interface augmentation for Vite
```

**Implementation Order:**
1. `types.ts` — Define all types first; everything depends on them.
2. `env.d.ts` — Augment ImportMeta for VITE_API_BASE_URL type safety.
3. `api.ts` — Implement resolveBaseUrl (read VITE_API_BASE_URL, strip trailing slash, default to empty string), parseErrorResponse (handle JSON/non-JSON/network errors → ApiError), and the five API functions using native fetch with typed returns.
4. `StatusBadge.tsx` — Stateless, no dependencies beyond types.
5. `TaskForm.tsx` — Controlled form, accepts TaskFormProps (onSubmit callback, optional initial Task).
6. `TaskItem.tsx` — Renders a Task, contains StatusBadge, exposes edit/delete via props callbacks.
7. `TaskList.tsx` — Maps tasks array to TaskItem components, keyed by task.id.
8. `App.tsx` — Wires everything: state (tasks, loading, error), useEffect with AbortController, handleCreate/handleUpdate/handleDelete (each calls API then refetches), renders TaskForm + TaskList + error banner.

**Key Decisions:**
- Native fetch over axios (zero dependencies, sufficient for this scope).
- Refetch-after-mutate over optimistic updates (simpler, correct, adequate for task management).
- Controlled form components over react-hook-form (2-3 fields don't justify the dependency).
- AbortController in useEffect cleanup for correctness under StrictMode.
- All API functions throw ApiError on failure; callers catch and set error state.
alternatives_considered: axios instead of native fetch — rejected: adds a dependency for no material benefit given the simple request patterns (no interceptors, no upload progress needed). Native fetch is well-supported in all target browsers.

React Query / TanStack Query for server state — rejected for initial implementation: adds significant complexity and a dependency. The manual useState + refetch-after-mutate pattern is adequate for a single-resource CRUD app. Can be introduced later if caching, background refetch, or pagination are needed.
react-hook-form for TaskForm — rejected: the form has only 2-3 fields. Controlled components with useState are simpler and keep the dependency count low.
Zustand or Redux for global state — rejected: a single App component managing tasks state is sufficient. No cross-cutting state concerns exist.
Optimistic updates — deferred: adds rollback logic and error-state complexity. Refetch-after-mutate is correct and perceptually fast for small datasets. Can be layered in later.

String literal union type ('pending' | 'in_progress' | 'done') vs enum for TaskStatus — either works; recommend string literal union as it avoids TypeScript enum pitfalls (no reverse mapping needed, better tree-shaking).
risks: CORS misconfiguration: If the backend doesn't set Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the frontend's origin, all API calls will fail. Ensure the FastAPI backend has CORSMiddleware configured. The frontend cannot fix this.

Stale base URL after build: Vite statically replaces import.meta.env at build time. If the API URL changes post-deployment, a rebuild is required. Mitigation: support a runtime config endpoint or inject via window.__CONFIG__ at serve time.

Race condition on rapid mutations: If a user creates/deletes tasks rapidly, refetch-after-mutate calls may resolve out of order, showing stale state. Mitigation: use an incrementing request ID or AbortController to cancel superseded fetches.

Missing error feedback: If parseErrorResponse doesn't handle all edge cases (e.g., 502 with HTML body from a reverse proxy), the user sees a cryptic or missing error message. Mitigation: always provide a fallback message string in parseErrorResponse.
File size creep: App.tsx with all handlers, state, and JSX could approach 300 lines. Mitigation: extract hooks into a custom useTaskApi() hook if needed.
No offline/retry handling: Network failures surface as errors with no automatic retry. Acceptable for MVP but should be noted as a future improvement.
compliance_notes: All files must remain under 300 lines per operating procedures. The proposed 7-file structure ensures this; App.tsx is the most at risk and should be monitored.
Composition over inheritance is satisfied: all components are functional components composed via props. No class components or inheritance hierarchies.
Type annotations: TypeScript enforces this naturally. All props interfaces, API function signatures, and return types will be explicitly typed.
The operating procedures mandate backend tests with pytest. Frontend tests are not explicitly required but are recommended. Vitest tests for api.ts functions would provide high-value coverage.
The frontend does not directly connect to PostgreSQL or use DATABASE_URL; it communicates exclusively through the FastAPI HTTP API.
TaskStatus enum values must exactly match the backend's Python enum to avoid serialization mismatches. Coordinate with backend TaskStatus definition.
